note: Independent reviewer, 12 stills (8 rooms, a shop, 3 fight frames), target Hollow Knight. Biggest lever: one character and foe art pass (matching hero, real boss creatures). Caveat: the 'beige hero' defect in the fight frames is the Barkbalm sheen the capture turned on, not the hero's normal look. The loop's own rubric for pass 492 is 96.8/100.
defects: Image 08 (Evercrown heart gate): cyan crystal spikes read as stamped over the foes and hide their silhouettes.
The Haar Wyrm reads as placeholder geometry: flat green circles with box heads on chains of discs.
Fight frames: the hero looks washed out next to exploration shots (partly the capture's Barkbalm sheen).
High Boughs: smooth high-resolution branches behind chunky pixel tiles look like two games layered.
The same domed hut repeats across biomes, and town rooms are flat corridors with townsfolk in a row.
Noisy checkerboard brick ceilings and floors frame every room in the same heavy rectangle.
Gnarlmaw's title card is faint and low-contrast.
Characters are about 30 px tall on a 540 px frame with little presence against large empty backdrops.

note: Independent reviewer, 12 stills (9 zone rooms, a shop, 2 guardians), target Hollow Knight, no hints. Up from 4.1 at pass 492. Reads as mid-tier indie, not hand-crafted: flat tile grids, flat lighting, a hero sprite far below the environment's fidelity. Fastest wins named: upgrade the player sprite, add contact shadows/AO where platforms meet walls, tile variants plus stronger atmospheric-perspective depth between the play layer and parallax. The loop's own rubric for pass 497 is 96.9/100.
defects: Player character fidelity gap: the hero is a small, soft, low-detail hooded figure with no readable silhouette or gear detail, far below the environment art.
Flat lighting with no ambient occlusion: walls meet floors and platforms meet backgrounds with hard, unshaded seams; light sources rarely cast gradient pools or contact shadows.
Visible tile repetition and grid banding: brick and wall fields tile obviously, with little tile variation, damage, or hand-placed detail to break the grid.
Foreground and background collapse to the same depth plane: trunks, mid platforms and the play layer share similar value and saturation, so the player can get lost against busy backdrops.
Boxy, framed rooms with dead space: many rooms are rectangles bounded by a thick wall border with large empty centers.
Over-reliance on halftone/dot-screen gradient fills standing in for real rendering, flattening large areas.
Generic, undersized foes with weak silhouettes.
Platforms are one uniform stamped plank sprite repeated across every biome.

note: Independent reviewer, 12 no-hints stills (9 zone rooms, a shop, 2 boss-arena frames), target Hollow Knight. CAVEAT: the two boss-arena frames rendered with no boss visible (a capture artifact on our side — the boss did not spawn in the static shot), so Characters-and-foes (3.0) and Combat-readability (2.6) are understated and this 4.2 overall is NOT like-for-like with pass-497's 5.3, which used live-guardian stills. The environment read is the fair signal for this pass (rim/AO shading): Environments 5.0, Atmosphere/lighting 5.6, Art cohesion 4.3. Reviewer praised the fog/lighting (haar_lampwick, the mire) and the clean shop UI; the biggest lever named is characters/foes — a large, readable, animated player and bosses that actually appear in frame.
defects: Capture artifact (not a game defect): both boss-arena frames showed the player in an empty room with no boss, so there was nothing to read or telegraph.
A uniform dot/crosshatch dither grid is laid over the midground on several rooms (boughs, evercrown, spires, sky_spring, sunken, vorrhallow), reading as flat moire noise rather than texture or depth.
In the sunlit bough room the background branches/leaves are translucent glass shapes at inconsistent scale, detached from the solid foreground, so the space reads as two unrelated layers.
The player sprite is tiny, low-detail and identical in pose across frames, with a muddy silhouette that never reads clearly against busy or dark backgrounds.
Platforms are the weakest geometry: sky_spring's floating bars are flat untextured solid-green rectangles and the wooden planks repeat as one stamped tile everywhere.
The grass fringe on floors and ledges is a single flat bright-green band with no shading or variation, cheapening otherwise-moody rooms (haar_lampwick, deep_roots, source_hall).
Enemies are nearly absent and when present are small and low-contrast, lost against the detailed background instead of popping as threats.
Heavy silhouette repetition: evercrown_heart and hearthroot_plaza tile the same rounded-headstone pillar across the whole screen, flattening the sense of a designed space.

note: Independent reviewer, 12 no-hints stills (9 zone rooms across heartwood/hearthroot/tower/haar/boughs/spires/sunken/vorrhallow/evercrown, a shop, and 2 live boss-arena frames: Haar Wyrm and Gnarlmaw), target Hollow Knight. Bosses were in frame this time, so this is like-for-like with pass-497's 5.3 (and up from it), unlike the environment-only pass-500 4.2 which had the boss-missing capture artifact. This pass (501) shipped atmospheric perspective on the parallax back layers; the reviewer read real depth cues and a consistent palette across biomes but named the same structural levers as the top defects: bosses that don't read as creatures, dead empty midgrounds, a tiny generic hero, flat directionless lighting, and enemies camouflaged against their tiles. The boss and hero items are the gated PixelLab art loop (awaiting Sean); the empty-rooms, lighting and enemy-contrast items are code-first and unblocked.

Independent reviewer, 12 no-hints stills (9 zone rooms across heartwood/haar/spires/boughs/evercrown/vorrhallow/sunken/tower/hearthroot, a shop, and 2 guardian showcase frames: Gnarlmaw and the Haar Wyrm), target Hollow Knight. This pass (502) softened the sky backdrop dither into a palette ramp with noise-dithered seams, killing the halftone/screen-door moire that was a top defect at the pass-497/500/501 grades. That defect is gone from this reviewer's list — he named depth in 02/04/09 backdrops and did not flag midground moire. Not strictly like-for-like with pass-501's 5.4: this set swapped the two live boss-arena frames for two guardian showcase frames, which the reviewer read harshly as placeholder-grade bosses (the gated PixelLab art loop), pulling Characters/Combat down. Top defects now are the gated items (forgettable hero, placeholder bosses) plus code-first/unblocked ones already queued (empty under-decorated rooms, flat ambient lighting, repetitive platform sprites, zone-to-zone palette/outline incoherence).

Pass 503 (grass fringe). Best recent number; the environment/atmosphere read carries it (Atmosphere 6.5, Environments 6). Reviewer confirmed the fringe is improved but still flags grass/ground transitions mildly among tiling-repeat notes, and the headline defects stay the gated art: the boss (shot 10) reads placeholder-grade and the hero is tiny/low-contrast. New code-first defect: ambiguous translucent teal foreground blocks in evercrown/drift_well look like unstyled collision/glass placeholders. Set swaps two live boss frames for guardian-arena showcase frames, so Characters/Combat are understated vs a live-boss set.

Pass 504 (tileset variants / grid banding). Up a touch from pass 503's 5.5; Atmosphere 6.5 and Art cohesion 6.0 carry it. The tiling-repetition defect dropped off the headline but still lands at #3 — the reviewer now points it at the backdrop brick (hearthroot, a parallax/mid-ground wall this pass did not touch) and the regular mortar lattice, not the solid-field accent repeat the variants broke. Headline defects stay the gated art: the boss (shot 10) reads placeholder-grade and the hero/foes are low-detail. New code-first defect: the recurring gray note/sign panels with meaningless scribble-lines (lore tablets / sign prompts) read as un-authored UI stubs across five rooms. The natural companion to this pass is a mid-ground/backdrop variant pass (vary <zone>_mid.png so its brick/column field stops repeating).

Pass 505 (per-zone distance-fog colour). Blind grader; 5.2 is within the recent 5.1-5.6 spread (variance between cold graders is real) and not a regression from this pass -- it explicitly reads the zone palettes as 'distinct' (murky swamp, purple crystal, dark forest, brick ruins, canopy, clockwork), and praises the town (05) and shop UI (10) as near-shipping. The drag is the gated art: the boss frame (11) reads off-spec/placeholder, the hero is a tiny low-detail blob that blows to white, and foes are too small to read -- all PixelLab items held on Sean's base approvals. The grey note/sign placeholder panels (already queued) and empty negative space (queued) recur. New code-first signal: the swamp (haar) and underwater (sunken) zones collapse into low-contrast grey-green/grey-teal so platforms and hazards don't separate from the backdrop -- partly this pass's dark haar/sunken fog; worth lifting gameplay-tile contrast or easing those two hazes.

Pass 510 (foreground silhouette layers). Blind grader on 11 shots across 7 zones + a shop + the Wyrm arena; 5.4 is within the recent 5.1-5.6 spread and not a regression (a different random shot spread, more character/empty-room heavy than pass 504's set). Atmosphere & lighting is the strongest area (6.5): it reads the point lights, fog, rain, grade and glow pools as 'real mood'. The new foreground wasn't singled out (it's a subtle near-black band by design), but depth/empty-space and flat-parallax notes persist, so 'more parallax layers' is the right next depth step. The drag stays the gated PixelLab art: the hero/NPCs read as tiny featureless blobs (#1 defect) and foes blend into their tiles. New non-gated defect: the coarse-pixel shop/HUD UI clashes with the finer in-world art and reads placeholder.

Pass 515 (second masonry sweep). Blind grader, 10 shots across 8 zones + a shop, no hints. 4.3 is below the recent 5.1-5.6 spread, from a harsher grader and a shot set heavy on tall rooms with large dark empty upper bands (heartwood amber_falls, haar, evercrown) that it read as a 'letterbox'. Verified: not a render bug but a real sparse/dark upper backdrop with thin parallax (aligns with Sean's depth/more-parallax request). Strongest: atmosphere/lighting 5.5 and the Market shopfronts; closest to the bar: Sunken and Vorrhallow silhouettes (the swept masonry zones). Weakest called: dark empty upper voids, remaining stamp repetition in Spires brick and Hearthroot background buildings, painterly-vs-flat-tile zone incohesion, and the player sprite.

Pass 520 (zone style cohesion: Heartwood/Haar sculpted mossy crown + mottled wood face). Blind grader, 10 shots across 8 zones, no hints, no HUD in the shots (captured without --ui, so its 'no HUD/UI 2.0' is a capture artifact, not a real defect). 4.7 sits in the recent 4.1-5.6 spread. Top real defects it raised: painterly/anti-aliased backdrops vs hard pixel foreground (the recurring style-incoherence theme this pass chipped at from the tile side), copy-pasted floating plank platforms with no structural support, cheap radial-gradient lantern/mushroom glow that ignores surfaces, and the small placeholder hero (the gated HD-hero/guardian art loop). Atmosphere/lighting its strongest axis (6.0).

Pass 525 spread (8 zones + shop). Up from 4.7. Top defects: tile repetition in stone/brick columns and gameplay masonry; style incoherence (soft vector swamp vs hard pixel tilesets); crushed-black dead zones (upper bands of dark rooms); weak/small character + foe presence; dark-on-dark hazard readability; flat tiling water/cattail fields.

Pass 529 spread (9 whole-room overviews across zones, 2 play-framed hit frames, a shop). Down from 5.6, on a different shot set: whole-room overviews this time where pass 525 framed at play scale, and the two hit frames threw a spark with no swing (the capture's --spark), caught on the sheet's opening disc. Top defects: foreground posts cut through actors (the Hearthroot shopkeepers); the hit spark's flat yellow disc covers the target and the blade; noisy high-frequency terrain fill with no clear lit top edge; random square 'missing pixel' blocks in midground ruins; one plank platform reused in every zone; shop footer gold differs from the HUD and the town backdrop differs between room and shop.

Pass 535 spread (8 zones at play scale with the HUD, 2 swing frames, the Hearthroot arms shop). Level with pass 529. Top defects: foreground silhouettes stand over the play layer as black bars (01, 04, 07-10); the new swing smear read fat, banana-yellow and ahead of the blade on one heavy frame (retuned slimmer and paler in the same pass; timing vs the windup queued); rooms are empty boxes of unsupported floating planks; placeholder set pieces (Spires red orb columns, grey sign slabs, flat liquid and crystal shapes); hero detail density and flat glow-disc lighting don't match the tiles.

Pass 540 spread (9 zones at play scale with the HUD, a swing frame, the Hearthroot arms shop). Up from 4.6 at pass 535. Top defects: rooms read as one template (spawn at the left edge beside a stele, rope-hung planks, an empty middle); flat placeholder props (Spires magenta islands, Evercrown hot-magenta platforms, the smelter's vector cauldron, the Haar's orange blocks); repeating tile stripes and grids, and the thorn column repeats one stamp; mixed rendering (painterly Boughs leaves, banded ring light pools); the hero is small and low-contrast; thin UI (shop with no icons, minimap a single rectangle, stray black bars in the shop).

Pass 545 spread (10 rooms across nine zones as whole-room views with the HUD, the Hearthroot arms shop). Up from 5.3 at pass 540. Top defects: off-room solid mass reads as flat repeated cobble with no falloff (Proving Scar); the Sunken Spring's stone pillars read as striped wallpaper and its water is a flat fill; layouts are empty boxes of hung planks in every zone; low-effort backgrounds (Hearthroot silhouettes, the Boughs' filtered foliage); the hero barely reads (small, low contrast, whole-room framing); fire seals lack glow onto nearby surfaces; Haar lamp lights stack as perfect circles; the shop has no icons or portrait; flat wading-water rectangles in Vorrhallow; uniform rain over the Spires.

Pass 550 spread (9 zone rooms as whole-room views with the HUD, the Hearthroot arms shop, the Haar Wyrm and Gnarlmaw fight frames). Level with pass 540, a tenth below 5.4 at pass 545. Atmosphere 6.5 is the strongest area; the reviewer's biggest levers are the code-drawn guardians (Haar Wyrm as flat circles, Gnarlmaw's repeated segments), the small hero, empty box rooms and loud repeating frame tiles.
defects: The Haar Wyrm reads as placeholder: flat identical teal circles and a blocky head with a pasted-on eye.
Gnarlmaw is a long row of identical segments that hides the hero and the safe space.
The hero is about 40 px tall and blends into backgrounds; no strong silhouette.
Rooms are wide empty rectangles with a flat floor and a few floating planks.
Frame tiles repeat on a loud grid (Tower and Vorrhallow checkered stone, Heartwood/Boughs striped dirt) and overpower the playfield.
Proving Scar: over half the screen is empty black void, and the lava column is a flat noisy rectangle with no glow falloff.
Foes (bee, snake, Bark Knight) are more saturated and detailed than the muted rooms, so they look pasted in.
The shop is a plain box with no item icons or portrait; the HUD is small and generic.

note: Pass 555 spread (9 zone rooms as whole-room views, the Hearthroot arms shop, the Haar Wyrm and Gnarlmaw fight frames). Down from 5.3 at pass 550 with a different room set (the Haar's drowned stair in fog and rain, the Trials, the Sunken aqueduct). The frame tiles no longer draw a checkerboard remark, but brick fields still read as a flat tile-editor fill with random dark missing bricks. Strongest: the Heartwood's mood (teal glow lights, hanging roots, light shafts).
defects: The Haar Wyrm frame: a near-black blob on a near-black arch with four yellow dashes for eyes; no silhouette, no visible hero, no telegraph.
Haar drowned stair: fog and rain wash the room to grey mud, with dither halos around lamps and platforms that barely read as walkable.
Spires, Vorrhallow, Sunken, Trials: terrain is a flat repeated brick with a hard black outline and random dark missing-brick noise; no structure, trim or wear.
Every room: a rectangular box with thin floating planks, a large empty middle, and almost no foreground, props or set dressing.
Gnarlmaw: one body segment tiled about 25 times in a row; the hero overlaps it dark red on dark brown; egg sacs and maw look pasted on.
Boughs: the smooth vector-style leaf backdrop clashes with the pixel tiles, and the saturated orange frame fights the green scene.
Foes come from different style families with inconsistent outline weight and shading.
The hero is small and stiff with a muted cloak and no signature shape, less detailed than the knight NPC.
Vorrhallow and Evercrown are nearly monochrome with low value contrast; shards, tendrils and columns blur together.
The shop has a large dead area between its rows and the description; the portrait is flatter than the world; the HUD masks are generic.

note: Pass 560 spread (9 zone rooms, the Hearthroot arms shop, the Gnarlmaw arena and the Haar Wyrm close-up). Up from 4.2 at pass 555 with a similar set. The Evercrown and Vorrhallow no longer draw the 'monochrome' remark; the brick remark is now tile repetition without trim, not noise. No frame shows an attack or a hit. Strongest: the Tower's smelter, a tilted crucible pouring molten metal, warm light on cool stone, the one room that feels composed.
defects: Seven rooms: the hero stands idle in one pose at the far left, tiny against the room; no frame shows animation, an attack arc or hit feedback.
Boughs canopy: flat saturated vector-like leaves and smooth branch curves behind chunky pixel tiles; white dash wind lines and a row of identical red thorn bulbs look like placeholders.
Haar marsh road: coarse dither halos around every lamp, pale vertical smears over the frame, and platforms, the crate and the spike bed nearly the same grey-green as the backdrop.
Gnarlmaw: one brown husk segment stamped about twenty times in a straight line with three flat yellow sacs; a tiled strip, not a creature, and the red hero is lost against it.
Sunken aqueduct: two thirds of the frame is a flat teal water gradient with dither banding, one small fish, and plain brick with an obvious repeat.
Heartwood, Vorrhallow, Evercrown, Tower: one terrain tile repeated without variation in thick floor and ceiling bands, with no edge pieces, cracks or trim.
Hearthroot plaza and shop: a flat low-contrast silhouette band behind a large empty mid-ground; crates and the doorway look pasted on, with no grounding shadows.
Spires sky steps: uniform white rain over everything competes with the foreground; small foes and pickups are lost on busy purple; the red bulb columns are one sprite about fifteen times each.
Vorrhallow: magenta shards scattered at random angles like floating spears, attached to no rock; the foe at the waterline is nearly invisible against the dark pillars.
The shop panel is legible but generic, with a large empty middle and a portrait simpler than the world sprites; the Haar Wyrm close-up is two pairs of yellow slits and grey puffs.

note: Pass 565 spread (9 zone rooms, the Hearthroot arms shop, and three fight frames: Heartwood hit, Vorrhallow tell, Tower hit). Down from 4.9 at pass 560; this is the first set with fight frames, and they drew two of the top four defects. The 'one tile with no trim' remark is gone for the Heartwood, Vorrhallow and the Evercrown; the Tower's plates still read as a noisy grid and the Sunken Spring's brick as uniform. Strongest: atmosphere in the dark zones (the root cavern's mushrooms and hanging lights, the foundry's crucible, the violet crystal ruin and its waterline).
defects: Boughs thorn-pit room: huge flat vector-style leaves, branches and white dash wind lines at a different style and pixel density from the sprites and tiles; reads as a pasted illustration.
Haar marsh road: full-screen fog streaks with coarse dithered halo blobs wash out platforms, the chest and the foreground; hard to tell what is solid.
The hero is tiny, stiff and upright in one idle pose at the left edge of almost every room, with a muddy green cloak and little silhouette character.
Both hit frames (Heartwood, Tower): the sword is a flat grey-white bar wider than the hero with no arc, smear or shading, and the struck foe is a solid white cutout; reads as a debug overlay.
Nearly every room uses one kit (rope or chain swings, a four-legged table platform, one chest) on a dead-flat floor; zones differ by palette more than architecture.
Sunken aqueduct: brick repeats uniformly with no edge wear or moss, the waterfall is a flat cyan strip, the underwater area an empty dithered gradient with one fish.
Spires sky steps: dense white rain at one brightness over everything, the red thorn-pod columns are one sprite tiled, the clouds are flat blobs against pixel tiles.
Tower: ceiling and floor are a noisy grid of small square plates with scattered dark squares; reads as a test pattern and competes with the crucible.
Shop: a plain dark rectangle, a three-item list leaving over half the panel empty, a crude portrait with heavier outlines than the rest of the game, tiny icons; small generic HUD.
Foes are small, low-detail and at inconsistent outline weights; the dark armored figure sinks into the dark foundry and the mantis-like foe into the jungle bridge.

note: Pass 570 spread (9 zone rooms: Hearthroot plaza, Heartwood lantern grotto, Haar Lampwick causeway, Boughs canopy bridge, Spires storm ledge, Tower Gear Pit, Vorrhallow drowned nave, Evercrown veins, Sunken spring gate; the Kettleforge smith's shop; two fight frames: Boughs hit, Haar tell). Up from 4.6 at pass 565. The grader, given no hints, named the Gear Pit the best frame: 'the large rusted gears give a real focal point, a sense of place and layered depth that the other rooms lack'. Also strong: each zone's controlled palette, the lanterns and glowing mushrooms, the Spires' rain and lightning, and a clean legible font and shop layout. UI rose to 5.0 from 4.4.
defects: Haar (Lampwick causeway, the tell frame): the fog is a full-screen layer of smeared vertical blobs that washes out platforms, the chest, spikes and foes; a dirty lens instead of depth.
Boughs (canopy bridge, the hit frame): smooth vector-like leaves and hairline branches at a different pixel density from the chunky tiles and sprites.
Hearthroot plaza and Evercrown veins: mostly empty dark space with flat silhouette backdrops and a handful of tiny props; no midground, no focal point.
The hero is a tiny, stiff, upright figure with little silhouette character, lost against the room scale (worst in the plaza, the Gear Pit and the veins).
Foes are small and low in contrast against their backgrounds (the knights in the drowned nave, the beetle on the storm ledge, the mantises in the Boughs), none with a memorable shape.
Light halos use a coarse checkerboard dither with hard stepped edges, clashing with the soft light shafts in the same frames (Haar, Vorrhallow).
Boughs hit frame: the sword is a flat grey slab longer than the hero with no shading; the hit spark and the foe's flash merge into one pale blob.
Tiles repeat in an obvious grid with blotchy dark stains instead of built structure (the Sunken sand brick, the plain stone squares of the Tower and the Spires).
Hazards and liquids are crude: the red thorn bulbs are one sprite stamped in a row, the Heartwood grotto's amber pool is a flat rectangle, the Haar's lava column a noisy strip with no glow shape.
The shop panel is a flat dark box with a thin border, no ornament and loose empty space; the white wind dashes in the Boughs read as a rendering glitch.

note: Pass 575 spread (9 rooms: Hearthroot plaza, Heartwood Rot Dwarf Hall, Tower Ore Bin and Rail Gallery, Haar Lampwick causeway, Boughs canopy bridge, Vorrhallow drowned nave, Sunken spring gate, Evercrown veins; the Kettleforge smith's shop; two fight frames: Tower hit, Haar tell). Up from 4.7 at pass 570. The grader, given no hints, said the large props carry the game: the pouring crucible (the best frame), the ore hopper, the trestle rail and the root splitting the high seat 'each give a room a subject and a story'. Also strong: each zone's own palette and material, the drowned nave and the Dwarf Hall as the moodiest frames, and a clean shop panel. The worst frame is again the Lampwick causeway under the Haar's fog.
defects: Rooms are flat boxes with one walkable strip: a rectangular tile frame around a dead-level floor with 60 to 70 percent empty dark air (plaza, Rail Gallery, Ore Bin, Dwarf Hall, veins). Vary the floor height, break the ceiling line, add foreground that overlaps the frame.

Characters are too small and too low in contrast for the stage (the hero is about 7 percent of the screen height; the nave's knight, the canopy bridge's archer and mantis, the Dwarf Hall's dwarf melt into the background). Rim light or value separation for every actor.
The Haar's fog is a dithered overlay with vertical smears that cuts contrast to near zero (Lampwick causeway, the tell frame); the lantern holes are coarse checkerboard blobs.
The Haar tell frame: the foe turns into a flat white featureless silhouette, like a missing texture; no direction, weapon or reach.

The Tower hit frame: the slash is a huge flat bar like a plank and the struck foe flashes fully grey-white, so attacker, weapon and target are one clump; the impact ring is small; no HUD in either fight frame.
Mixed rendering styles: the Boughs' smooth vector-like leaves and white wind dashes, soft smudged shadow blotches over the spring gate's crisp brick.
Tiling repeats over large areas with no trim, cracks or large stones (the spring gate is half plain brick; the Tower's block grid; the canopy bridge's striped bark border).
NPCs and foes sit below the hero's standard: stiff front-facing shop people, a cartoonish purple blob in the Rail Gallery and the bee on the canopy bridge.
Hazards and pickups read unevenly: the red thorn row is one loud stamp, the causeway's spikes are near invisible, and the hanging chest platform is the same gimmick in five rooms.
Lighting is decorative, not structural: faint shafts that tint nothing, lanterns with no cast light on nearby tiles, the veins' monotone purple, the plaza's flat two-tone city cutout.

note: Pass 580 spread (8 rooms: Hearthroot plaza, Heartwood Hornet Gallery and Rot Dwarf Hall, Tower Rail Gallery and Ore Bin, Haar Lampwick causeway, Vorrhallow drowned nave, Sunken drowned aqueduct; the Hearthroot arms shop; three fight frames: Heartwood hit, Haar tell, Spires hit). Up from 4.8 at pass 575, the largest step so far; some of it may be the grader, a fresh one each time, so read it with the next grade. Room shape is no longer named as a defect. The grader, given no hints, again named the set pieces as the best of the game (the hornet nest, the ore hopper, the root-split high seat), then each zone's own palette, and the Heartwood hit frame's slash and burst. The worst frame is again the Lampwick causeway under the Haar's fog.
defects: The Haar's fog destroys readability and looks like an artifact (the causeway, the Haar tell frame): spikes, the chest and foes fall below visible contrast, and the lantern clearings are coarse dithered blobs. Put fog behind the play layer only, keep platforms, pickups and foes at full value, and make the lantern light a soft glow.

Characters are too small and too quiet for the frame (every room; worst in the plaza, the Rail Gallery and the aqueduct): the hero is about 6 percent of the screen height, and foes are dark on dark. Tighten the camera or enlarge the sprites, rim the hero, and give each foe one saturated color.
The sword in the hit frames is a flat white bar wider than the hero, and the struck foe hides behind the burst (Heartwood hit, Spires hit).
Large dead midgrounds and flat backdrops (the plaza's west half, the aqueduct's open water, the Rail Gallery).
Tile repetition that shows the grid (the aqueduct's sandstone, the Tower's ceilings, the Spires' floating blocks).
The shop panel is plain and oversized for its content, its portrait is cruder than the world, and the HUD overlaps the ceiling tiles.
The Spires fight frame is noisy: rain, lightning, lamps and magenta rock compete, and lightning crosses the harpy.

note: Pass 585 spread (8 rooms: Hearthroot plaza, Heartwood Rot Dwarf Hall, Boughs canopy bridge, Tower Gear Pit, Haar Lampwick causeway, Vorrhallow flooded hall, Spires storm ledge, Sunken drowned aqueduct; the Hearthroot arms shop; three fight frames: Heartwood tell, Haar hit, Spires hit). Down from 5.6 at pass 580 with a fresh grader and four different rooms, so read the two together: the game sits between 5 and 6. Combat readability rose to 5.5 (5.2): the Spires hit frame was named among the best things for its arc, spark and struck beetle 'even through rain' (pass 584), and the tell is no longer called a missing texture (pass 585), though the grader wants an outline only. Best frames again the set pieces: the Rot Dwarf Hall's root-split gate and the Gear Pit. The worst frame is again the Lampwick causeway under the Haar's fog.
defects: The Haar's fog is visual mud (the causeway, the Haar hit frame): the overlay flattens everything and the dithered holes around lamps look like rendering errors. Fog behind the play layer, half the opacity, soft gradient light.
Rooms are rectangular boxes (Boughs canopy bridge, Vorrhallow flooded hall, Spires storm ledge, Sunken aqueduct): flat ceilings, straight walls, one thick tile border.
The hero is small, stiff and low in presence, with less contrast than a chest (all rooms; worst in the plaza and the causeway).
Mixed rendering styles: smooth leaves and soft clouds behind crisp pixel tiles (Boughs, Spires), and a shop portrait cruder than the sprites.
Repeated set dressing: the same chest on a thin table and the same sign in nearly every room; red gem spikes that ignore their zone.
Dead midground (the plaza; the aqueduct's plain oversized brick and flat water).
The sword is a featureless white bar as long as the hero, and the tell's gold full-body tint erases the foe's form (flash only an outline or the weapon).
Thin UI: the shop is a plain dark panel with no frame ornament.

note: Pass 590 spread (the same rooms as pass 585: Hearthroot plaza, Heartwood dwarf hall, Boughs canopy bridge, Tower gear pit, Haar Lampwick causeway, Vorrhallow flooded hall, Spires storm ledge, Sunken drowned aqueduct; the Hearthroot arms shop; three fight frames: Heartwood tell, Haar hit, Spires hit). Level with 5.3 at pass 585 with a fresh grader. The four reshaped rooms are no longer called rectangular boxes, but their ceilings now read as stair-stepped tile blocks. Best frames again the Heartwood dwarf hall and its tell, the aqueduct and the gear pit. Combat readability fell to 4.5 (5.5): the hit frames' sword is a flat white plank with no smear and no flash on the foe.
defects: The hero and foes are tiny against the room (about 6% of screen height); zoom the camera 1.5 to 2x or scale the characters.
Hit frames have no impact (Haar hit, Spires hit): a flat white plank of a sword with no taper or smear, a small spark, no flash or knockback on the foe.
